\section{The same properties on a maze}
\label{sec:maze}
% =======================================================================================

A route task with the engine's integer judge is the harder test of the three properties: one
wrong action is a zero. We use a colour maze whose engine, solver and judge (legal moves,
reaching the target, staying within the step limit, key and door pickup rules) are imported unmodified
in every environment below, and whose judge's file hash is re-checked before any number.
% SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
\emph{Environment names are part of every result, and no two environments ever share a
table.}
\textbf{CMAZE-1} is the generator at its own defaults; \textbf{CMAZE-2} a request layer over it
that places named agents and targets across two door-free components and seals one target per
maze; \textbf{CMAZE-2b} CMAZE-2 with one acceptance rule added, \emph{keep a pair iff its optimal
route picks up at least two keys}; \textbf{CMAZE-T} and \textbf{CMAZE-O} the transition and
observation instruments whose rows are in Sec.~\ref{sec:maze-wm}.

\subsection{Fixing the request layer (CMAZE-2b)}
\label{sec:req-layer}

On CMAZE-2 the blind-sequential planner, which ignores key order, was valid on 0.9077 /
0.8905 / 0.9128 of held-out unseen-pair routes, against the published 0.4980 of CMAZE-1: 1,242
of 1,449 optimal routes picked up exactly one key, so there was no key order for the second rule
to trap. % SRC: w13-seeds-and-tables/TABLES.md
The cause was the layer's own acceptance test. A maze whose door cut needs two keys cannot
supply the reverse direction at all, because the key that opens the cut door lives on one side
of the cut, and the layer required pairs in both directions; the symmetry requirement selected
single-key cuts. % SRC: w14-request-layer-fix/FINAL-REPORT.md
CMAZE-2b adds one integer rule, keep a pair iff its optimal route takes at least two keys, and
changes nothing else: the fraction of routes needing at least two keys goes from 0.1428 to
1.0000, blind-sequential on held-out unseen pairs falls from 0.9077 to 0.1818--0.2344, and the
oracle stays at 1.0000 (Tabs.~\ref{tab:req} and~\ref{tab:req2b}, App.~\ref{app:verb}). % SRC: w14-request-layer-fix/FINAL-REPORT.md

The fix lands in CMAZE-1's own multi-key band rather than at its mixture value of 0.4980, and % SRC: w14-request-layer-fix/FINAL-REPORT.md
its side effects are declared (App.~\ref{app:verb}).

\subsection{Composition on routes: the verb is the lever, and it belongs to the interface}
\label{sec:verb}

The n-CLU's read is linear in the request design, so composing two half-addresses averages
their latents. An engine-judged route task composes by union: overlay the two decoded half-plans,
the target's plan winning conflicts. We hold everything fixed but the verb: the same n-CLU and
controls, the same request-only read, the same frozen encoder and shared decoder, the same
judge and split, and baselines at matched parameters, on CMAZE-2b, TEST, three scored seeds.
\texttt{AVG} decodes the average of the two half-latents (the earlier read on the identical two
latents); \texttt{MERGE} decodes each half and overlays the plans. Nothing in the verb is
fitted, and the address book is never refit for the halves. % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md

\paragraph{The verb claim.} Moving the composition of two half-addresses from latent space to
plan space, on identical latents and through the identical frozen decoder, lifts the n-CLU's
held-out unseen-pair validity by $+0.4422$ / $+0.5354$ / $+0.4471$ on three of three seeds, and
lifts the $n$-way conjunction row from 0.0000 / 0.0160 / 0.0000 to 0.4891 / 0.4652 / 0.3915.
% SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
The merge rule is load-bearing: on the identical two decoded plans, letting the agent's plan
win reads 0.2714 / 0.4848 / 0.4423, the agent half alone 0.1960 / 0.2424 / 0.2404 and the target
half alone 0.0704 / 0.1010 / 0.1202. % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
The geometry says why averaging cannot work: the two half-latents are nearly parallel,
$\cos(Z_A,Z_B)=0.9668$ / 0.9589 / 0.9630, and their average is aligned with the full read at
0.9971 / 0.9964 / 0.9966, so averaging returns a slightly shrunk copy of what the linear read
already gives; the latent space has no room for a union, while the same two halves decoded are
complementary in plan space. % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md

\paragraph{Why it is an interface claim and not an n-CLU claim.} The same fixed merge lifts every
arm that reads anything, and it lifts the matched-bytes lookup floor by $+0.8299$ against the
n-CLU's $+0.4749$, carrying that floor to 0.9648 / 0.9646 / 0.9808 on unseen pairs, past the
n-CLU and past the single-decode pipeline ceiling. % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
The pre-declared landscape controls do not collapse: on the seen row landscape shuffled reads 0.5111
/ 0.5552 / 0.5727 and random atoms 0.5395 / 0.5650 / 0.5858, against a collapse bar of
half the n-CLU's score, 0.3606 / 0.3455 / 0.3508. % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
So no row is claimed for the n-CLU, on either verb. The verb claim survives because
\texttt{MERGE} and \texttt{AVG} consume the same two latents: a verb claim is not an n-CLU claim,
and only the verb claim is made. The composition operator is part of the \emph{interface} and it
is task-shaped: images compose by mixing latents; routes compose by overlaying constraints.

\paragraph{The lookup floor, printed honestly.} The floor reaches about 0.97 because it is not a
compressed baseline: at this configuration the n-CLU's read size holds more latents than the split
has training items, so the matched-bytes lookup \emph{is} the whole training set of routes
through the evaluation mazes (369,152 / 366,080 / 371,456 floats). % SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
It is the \emph{within-maze} floor. It cannot transfer across mazes: a fragment table built from
other mazes' routes, the published tripwire, reads exactly 0.0000 at $r=1$ and $r=2$ on every
CMAZE-2b bank, while the same-maze fragment table reaches 0.4829 to 0.5692 at $r=2$.
% SRC: w14-request-layer-fix/FINAL-REPORT.md
The two-decode merge is not bounded by the single-decode pipeline ceiling, which bounds an arm
that emits one latent and decodes once; the lookup exceeds it by $+0.2740$ to $+0.3216$ on
unseen pairs, with no leak, both halves reading training latents only.
% SRC: w14-read-verb/FINAL-REPORT.md
The n-CLU's differentiator on the maze is therefore deletion, which transferred
(Tab.~\ref{tab:maze-del}); the composition result on routes belongs to the verb.
